question: Which undamped degree-2 modes account for the depth-seven finite-window gap?

objects.definition: Differential and constant boundary transform sectors on zI+B3^T B3

objects.units: squared native angular frequency for z
objects.basis_orientation: coherent top orientations; ascending boundary labels

objects.definition: Normalized dual pole mass divided by its positive eigenvalue and times midpoint cosine mean

technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: Identify individual accessible modes and net grade contributions

calculation_steps: Deduce constants and differential sectors from coherent dual Gram
Derive the two scalar recursion formulas
Bracket selected roots and differentiate their Schur functions using interval arithmetic
Compare their contributions with numerical Fourier sector means

result.exact_expression: The depth-seven target is exactly edge-free. Two interval-verified constant-terminal modes contribute +0.083500 and +0.033991; the differential sector offsets part of the positive top-cell transient.
result.approximation: Net top-cell transient +0.055292, total gap estimate +0.084735
result.precision_and_error: Selected frequencies enclosed with widths < 1e-11; their contrast intervals have widths < 1e-7. Whole-sector means are numerical diagnostics.
result.scope: Undamped uniform d=7; three isolated boundary-accessible poles, no complete pole enumeration

verification.method: Shallow dual checks, exact outer closure, interval pole conditions, and numerical Fourier sums

counterexamples_and_failures: Target edge channel is identically zero on the tested exterior pattern; the positive transient can be traced to top-cell modes without assuming high-frequency localization.
limitations: No measured or damped spectral attribution.
changed_dependencies: New exact scalar dual-terminal reduction for the top-cell channel.
next_discriminant: Lift the selected eigenvectors and measure their norm distribution by refinement level and cell orbit.
